newsitem.title: BELGIUM: East Timor activist urges Indonesia arms sales ban.
newsitem.headline: East Timor activist urges Indonesia arms sales ban.

text.p: East Timor human rights activist Jose Ramos-Horta said on Monday that leading nations should freeze arms sales to Indonesia and warned that the country probably faced a period of political instability.

"I make a strong appeal to the European Union and United States to freeze for the next three or five years any weapons sales to the government of Indonesia because there are going to be changes...the regime is getting old," Horta told a news conference at the Belgian Parliament.
"From a strategic point of view, it is extremely dangerous to provide weapons to a dictatorship that is under challenge," Horta, the co-holder of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize, added.

Indonesia's 75-year-old President Suharto has ruled since 1967 when he seized power at the head of the army. Last week the state news agency quoted him as saying he was in good health, apparently in an effort to quash rumours to the contrary circulating on financial markets.

Horta was speaking after a meeting with European Union Commission President Jacques Santer on the first day of a three-day visit to Brussels to address Belgian and EU officials about East Timorean demands for democracy.
Horta praised EU nations for supporting a resolution adopted by the United Nations Human Rights Commission on April 16 criticising Indonesia over alleged army killings in East Timor since 1993.
On Tuesday Horta is due to address members of the European Parliament, which is presently debating a proposal that arms sales to developing nations be governed by a code of conduct.

Horta said Belgium has said it will not sell weapons to Indonesia, whose army invaded East Timor, a former Portuguese colony, in 1975. But he criticised other western countries for apparent double standards.
"We find it totally unacceptable that big western democracies who are most vocal about human rights are the biggest suppliers of arms to dictatorships like Indonesia," Horta said.
Germany announced last week it was negotiating to sell Indonesia four submarines.
